summary: Add manifest-driven OAuth authorization-code/PKCE and client-credentials metadata, exact callback binding, one-time tenant state, encrypted token exchange and DNS-pinned credential-aware remote probes without importing provider implementations into the host runtime.

impacts.evidence: OAuth sessions bind authenticated organization, workspace, actor and connector-account version and use forced PostgreSQL RLS.
PostgreSQL stores only state SHA-256 and opaque SecretProvider references; raw state, verifier, client secret and tokens remain encrypted and are revoked after use.
OpenAPI 0.14.0 adds two authenticated additive OAuth operations and regenerated SDK methods.
No domain event or canonical envelope changes.
Manifest v2 gains additive OAuth and connection-test metadata while the frozen Connector and Runtime interfaces remain unchanged.
Expand migration 000066 adds one-time OAuth sessions and the oauth_state secret class without changing existing account readers.
PKCE S256, cryptographic state, atomic consume, exact callback allowlist, actor/version binding, public-address DNS pinning, redirect denial and response/time bounds fail closed.
OAuth enrollment is audited write-sensitive; remote validation is read-safe and cannot activate an account.
Start, completion and connection validation record bounded audit actions without credential values or provider response bodies.
Start replays the exact encrypted pending state for one actor/correlation key; callback state is consumable once and account activation still requires a later healthy check.
New egress is limited to exact manifest HTTPS endpoints with DNS rebinding protection; redirects and private/special-use addresses are denied.
Remote failures map to bounded reason codes and never expose raw HTTP errors, tokens or bodies.
The previous binary can ignore migration 000066; session rows and encrypted evidence are retained until a reviewed contract migration.
PKCE, callback policy, secret parsing, migration invariants, manifest drift, route parity, contracts, SDK and frontend checks cover the change.
